if_else.title: if and else
if_else.big_idea: An if/else is a fork in the road: Python checks the condition once and runs exactly one of the two blocks, never both.
steps: Put the real value into the condition.
Decide True or False (careful: > is strict).
True: run the if block. False: run the else block.
if_else.sense_check: x = 5: is 5 > 5? No, they are equal, so the else block runs.

steps: Only the if block runs: big.

elif_chains.title: elif chains
elif_chains.big_idea: In an if/elif/else chain, Python runs the FIRST branch whose condition is True and skips the rest, even if a later branch would match 'better'. So the order of the checks matters.
steps: Check the conditions from top to bottom.
Stop at the first True one and run only that block.
If none are True, run the else block.
elif_chains.sense_check: score = 85 with 'if score > 50' first: 85 > 50 is True, so it prints pass, and the merit check never happens.

steps: That branch runs; the elif is skipped.
